critical_gates.description: systematic incidental or unsupported locator pattern
central subject or conclusion materially omitted
heading reverses or seriously misrepresents source stance
compound heading locators support only separate components
see source replaces a warranted substantive entry
unresolved, self-referential, circular, or chained cross-reference
systematic named-entity, example, or citation clutter
more than 1% of in-scope locator assignments uninspectable without a frozen alternative tolerance

strengths.summary: The normalized hierarchy is complete and shallow: all 1,904 delivered paths resolve to one terminal node, with 1,066 main headings and 838 second-level subheadings and no unresolved ownership.
Cross-chapter coherence is strong: 614 locator-bearing paths retrieve treatment from more than one intellectual unit while preserving stable complete-path identities.
Registered locator review supports 5,123 of 5,338 atomic assignments; display-to-atomic ownership remains exact for all 4462 delivered displays.
All four substitutive ‘see’ references resolve to substantive access without self-reference, cycles, chains, or loss of warranted direct access; ten additional see-also routes are fully supported.

Alphabetical navigation is coherent apart from conventional punctuation/name-order comparisons (8 machine flags reviewed as non-defects); mechanical faults are localized to the recorded accent substitutions and registered MEC findings.
